close_reason: Added doc-comment cross-references on the four collision-prone public structs (Calendar, EmailAddress, Address, Relation), mirroring the existing Link precedent. description:
Three workspace crates expose a type named Calendar with different shapes:

- jmap-jscontact-types::Calendar at crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs:507
  — JSContact calendaring resource (RFC 9553 §2.4.1)
- jmap-jscalendar-types — does not expose a Calendar type directly (uses
  JSCalendar entry types), but the package name suggests it
- jmap-calendars-types::Calendar — JMAP Calendars binding object, a
  separately-shaped wire type

A consumer doing 'use jmap_jscontact_types::Calendar; use
jmap_calendars_types::Calendar' immediately hits a name collision and must
alias. That is unavoidable given the spec naming.

What is avoidable: the crate documents this collision only on the Link type at
lib.rs:787-788 ('Distinct from JSCalendar's Link type'). Calendar — the more
likely collision — has no such note. Neither do Author (lib.rs:1064) or other
common-name types.

Fix: add a doc-comment cross-reference on Calendar pointing at
jmap_calendars_types::Calendar, with one line explaining the shapes differ.
Same pattern as the existing Link cross-reference. Repeat for any other
collision-prone names.

Caller-side impact is small but not zero: a consumer that imports
jmap_contacts_types::Calendar (which re-exports this Calendar) and writes a
function fn fetch_calendar() -> Calendar will be confused when their CalendarS
backend returns a different Calendar type. The doc cross-reference saves them
that confusion.
title: Calendar struct shares name with two other workspace crates — only Link's doc warns about the collision
